papers.title: A Full-Thickness 3D Bioprinted Melanoma-on-Chip Platform for Preclinical Therapeutic Testing
papers.abstract: Malignant melanoma remains a major clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and frequent therapy resistance. Although recent therapeutic advances have improved patient survival, predictive preclinical models that recapitulate the human tumor microenvironment (TME) remain limited. We developed a human 3D bioprinted melanoma-on-chip platform that combines a fully differentiated, barrier-forming human skin model with microfluidic perfusion and spatially controlled integration of melanoma spheroids at the epidermal-dermal junction. This provides a standardized tissue environment for longitudinal tumor and therapeutic studies for up to 21 days. To validate our model for preclinical therapeutic testing, we treated the melanoma-on-chip with the oncolytic virus VSV-GP. In 2D, viral infection of melanoma cells resulted in homogeneous cell death within 48 hours. In melanoma-on-chip, viral propagation was restricted to tumor cells and markedly delayed compared to 2D. Although VSV-GP stopped melanoma growth in 3D, it did not achieve complete tumor-cell eradication, as observed in 2D culture. These findings demonstrate that the 3D skin tissue environment substantially influences viral infection kinetics and therapeutic outcome, underscoring the need for more physiologically relevant human tissue models in preclinical drug evaluation.

papers.title: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates
papers.abstract: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction. Here, we present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that confines single cells in nanowells to obtain uniformly framed, regularized single-cell images, enabling MoA inference directly from raw images without segmentation or human-engineered features. Using a nanowell-in-microwell platform, we treated cells with 21 chemotherapeutic compounds spanning 11 MoA classes across multiple doses and time points, generating more than 500,000 single-cell images for model training and validation. A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network trained on images annotated by known compound mechanism achieved 85% accuracy in MoA classification. When a second model was trained on compound identity rather than MoA, misclassification patterns frequently linked compounds with shared mechanisms, indicating that the model learned mechanism-level relationships directly from single-cell morphology, without those relationships being specified in advance. Together, these results establish regularized single-cell imaging in nanowells as a scalable and interpretable approach to image-based MoA classification that overcomes key limitations of segmentation-dependent feature analysis.

papers.title: TEMPLE-MEASURED POSTPRANDIAL CARDIOVASCULAR RESPONSES UNDER FREE-LIVING CONDITIONS
papers.abstract: Eating perturbs cardiovascular homeostasis: splanchnic vasodilation after a meal is offset by autonomic adjustments that raise heart rate, and both the magnitude and duration of this response can depend on meal size and composition. Measuring these responses in daily life requires knowing when each meal begins and ends, which self-report captures poorly. The temple region allows both to be measured with a single device: chewing-related motion over the temporalis can mark meal onset and offset, and photoplethysmography (PPG) at the superficial temporal artery (STA) records the cardiovascular response. The STA also supplies a vascular bed whose postprandial behavior has not been well characterized. Using a temple-worn wearable under free-living conditions, we asked (1) whether established postprandial heart rate (HR) responses can be observed from automatically detected meals, and (2) how PPG pulse morphology at the STA changes after a meal. One meal from each of 100 participants in free-living conditions was analyzed, comparing a 15-min pre-meal baseline with the 120 min after eating, with nutrient content estimated from meal photographs. HR rose approximately 2.6 bpm on average in the first 15 min after eating and approached baseline within two hours. The postprandial rise in HR increased with caloric content. HR remained elevated two hours after the most sodium-dense meals, whereas higher fiber density was associated with a larger rise only during the first 15 minutes. The heart-rate increase per 100 kcal was greater in participants with higher BMI. In addition, the PPG morphology index A_d/A_a, a second-derivative PPG marker of vascular tone and wave reflection, increased within 15 minutes of the meal and remained shifted at two hours at the temple region. This change persisted after adjustment for heart rate and is consistent with reduced wave reflection, possibly associated with vasodilation in vessels downstream of the aorta. These results support the feasibility of using a single temple-worn device to detect meals and measure the cardiac and vascular responses that follow in daily life, and identify the temple as a site for studying postprandial vascular changes.

papers.title: Optimisation of GMP-compliant hollow-fiber culturing and scaled-up separation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles to overcome unexpected impact of bovine serum contaminants' transfer to end products
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) requires scalable manufacturing strategies ensuring product purity, reproducibility, and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. However, fetal bovine serum (FBS)-derived contaminants may persist in EV preparations, compromising their characterization and clinical applicability. This study aimed to optimize MSC-EV production using hollow-fiber bioreactors while minimizing bovine protein contamination through improved culture and purification strategies. Extracellular vesicles from immortalized human adipose-derived MSCs were produced under different culture conditions, including FBS supplementation, partial replacement with Panexin, and use of chemically defined medium for high-density cultures (CDM-HD). EVs were purified using tangential flow filtration, fast protein liquid chromatography, and ultrafiltration, and characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis, electron microscopy, Western blot, proteomics, and ELISA. Proteomic analysis revealed substantial bovine protein contamination under conventional FBS-containing conditions, with 11.4% of identified proteins exclusively assigned to bovine origin. Transitioning to CDM-HD reduced this proportion to 2.6%, markedly decreasing albumin abundance. Optimization of Panexin supplementation supported MSC expansion while reducing the necessary percentage of bovine serum. Although albumin became undetectable by Western blot, sensitive ELISA measurements revealed residual contamination and suggested unexpected protein carryover associated with chromatography column reuse. Importantly, using a new purification column yielded CDM-HD-derived EV preparations with albumin concentrations below ELISA assay's quantification limit (0.69 ng/mL). These findings highlight the importance of controlling both upstream culture conditions and downstream purification to prevent exogenous protein contamination, establishing a promising scalable manufacturing workflow for high-purity MSC-EVs suitable for further GMP-oriented development and future clinical translation.

papers.title: BMP-2 Release from Biomaterial Carriers: Reporting Heterogeneity and the Limits of Cross-Study Prediction
papers.abstract: Published release profiles offer a potential basis for predicting bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) delivery from biomaterial carriers, but heterogeneous reporting and study-specific effects complicate their reuse in machine learning (ML) models. As a preliminary exploration, we compiled 79 release experiments and 487 time points from 21 publications with a workflow that combined a large language model assistant and human verification, and we examined data comparability and cross-study prediction with ML models. Only 38 experiments (48%) reported BMP-2 alone as a percentage of the loaded dose. Within individual studies, binding components and coating layers were associated with slower release, consistent with established carrier mechanisms. Using carrier family as the sole predictor, a family-median model and gradient-boosted decision trees achieved lower mean absolute errors than a global-median baseline under random hold-out validation (0.42 and 0.44 versus 0.52 log10 units). Publication-grouped cross-validation did not establish a corresponding improvement (0.57 and 0.48 versus 0.50). Only 10 of the 28 modeling experiments belonged to carrier families represented in the training data under this scheme, and carrier family was strongly associated with publication. These findings highlight the need to distinguish within-study interpolation from cross-study generalization. Broader coverage of each carrier family, quantitative formulation and assay descriptors, and accessible numerical source data are needed to support predictive modeling of BMP-2 release.

papers.title: A One-Year In Vivo Study of a Braided Pure Molybdenum Stent: Favorable Biocompatibility and the Critical Challenge of Vascular Biomechanics
papers.abstract: Background: This study aims to evaluate a newly developed biodegradable stent made of pure Molybdenum (Mo) for treating intracranial aneurysms. Unlike traditional permanent metal stents that remain in the body indefinitely, this new device aims to provide temporary support during the healing process and then safely dissolve. Methods: A 30.48 {micro}m braided Mo stent was developed, and its mechanical performance and degradation process were tested in vitro. The stent was then implanted into the arteries of Beagle dogs for a one-year observation period. The study compared these new stents against standard non-degradable stents to monitor safety, structural changes, and the degradation rate within a living organism. Results: The Mo stents demonstrated excellent biocompatibility, showing no signs of organ damage or neurotoxicity, and the material degraded at a rate suitable for aneurysm healing (4.88-5.12 {micro}m/year). However, while the control stents held their shape, the Mo stents showed progressive structural deformation and recoil over time when implanted in the common carotid artery and subclavian artery of Beagle dogs. Conclusion: While this study confirms that Mo is a biocompatible material for stents, it highlights a major challenge in dynamic blood vessels. Future designs must focus on improving the stent's resistance to withstand the repetitive forces found in dynamic blood vessels before it can be considered for clinical use, and intracranial application still requires validation using aneurysm models in the future.

papers.title: RoWS Biofabrication of Neuromuscular Tubuloids from Human Neuromesodermal Progenitors
papers.abstract: Combining multicellular self-organization with defined tissue architecture remains a challenge in human neuromuscular modeling. Here, we use rotary wet-spinning (RoWS) biofabrication to encapsulate human neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) within fibrin-based cores surrounded by alginate shells, generating neuromuscular tubuloids (nmTubs). NMPs derived from a human embryonic stem cell and an induced pluripotent stem cell line were cultured for up to 50 days and assessed by gene expression analysis, immunofluorescence, tissue orientation measurements, and calcium imaging. Both cell lines generated muscle and neural compartments, with distinct differentiation kinetics and tissue proportions. Embryonic stem cell-derived nmTubs developed more extensive neural- and endothelial-associated structures and displayed spontaneous contractions from day 14 onward. Between days 30 and 50, muscle tissue area and myotube diameter increased, while acetylcholine receptor domains underwent spatial remodeling. Neural projections exhibited pronounced longitudinal organization within the constructs. Acetylcholine-associated calcium transients demonstrated tissue responsiveness, although functional neuromuscular transmission remains to be established. These findings show that RoWS can combine a common developmental progenitor population with a defined fibrous architecture to support multicellular neuromuscular development. nmTubs provide a platform to investigate the relationships among biomaterial geometry, tissue organization, and maturation in human neuromuscular models.

papers.title: Extracellular matrix-enriched human induced chondrocyte organoids as living building blocks for scalable cartilage tissue engineering
papers.abstract: Articular cartilage defects are common and often develop into painful and debilitating osteoarthritis due to the low innate healing capacity of cartilage. However, current regenerative treatments are limited as they depend on large autologous cell numbers and poor scalability. Here, a novel approach for rapid and plentiful cartilage organoid production is introduced for modular and scalable cartilage tissue engineering, by combining an off-the-shelf cell source with a natural matrix supplement in spinner flask cultures. First, human induced chondroprogenitor cell (hiCPC) colonies are matured towards human induced chondrocytes (hiCHO) aggregates in spinner flasks. Although maturation is achieved, resulting hiCHO aggregates show some phenotypic heterogeneity between clones. Nevertheless, subsequent dissociation and culture with a tissue-derived matrix supplement results in rapid and homogeneous organoid self-assembly, generating large numbers of hiCHO-derived cartilage organoids. This matrix-supplemented culture generates consistent pericellular and extracellular matrix-rich organoids without detected off-target cells, limiting the need of labor-intensive selections steps and enhancing scalability. Impressively, 1 million hiCHOs produce over 27,000 organoids within two weeks, with an approximately 30-fold increase in cell number. Finally, hiCHO-derived organoids fuse together to assemble large cartilage constructs, demonstrating their potential as scalable, off-the-shelf building blocks and addressing an unmet need in regenerative cartilage tissue engineering.

papers.title: Suprathreshold suppression underlies spatial selectivity in temporal interference stimulation
papers.abstract: Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) has been proposed for non-invasive deep-brain targeting using temporally interfering kilohertz-frequency electric fields, but the neuronal basis of its spatial selectivity remains unclear. Here we show that differential suppression of suprathreshold firing can support spatially selective recruitment. Multiscale simulations revealed no activation-threshold advantage for TIS over unmodulated high-frequency stimulation (HFS). At higher currents, HFS produced sustained depolarization and firing suppression, whereas strongly modulated TIS permitted periodic repolarization and maintained beat-locked firing. Spatially varying responses supported selective firing and current-ratio-dependent steering over an intensity-dependent range. Whole-cell recordings in mouse cortical slices under pharmacological synaptic blockade supported the predicted membrane-potential and firing dynamics. Retinal multielectrode-array recordings showed spatially patterned preservation of firing and current-ratio-dependent steering. In vivo intracortical stimulation in rats produced stronger beat-frequency locking of motor responses with a premodulated TIS waveform than with HFS. Our findings link suprathreshold neuronal response dynamics to spatial selectivity and characterize an intensity-dependent operating regime for TIS.

papers.title: A highly-parallel microchannel platform reveals the transcriptomic and epigenetic signature of confined migration
papers.abstract: Confining tissue microenvironments are ubiquitous in vivo, yet existing in vitro platforms are limited in geometric control, throughput, or compatibility with post-migration cell recovery. We developed a highly parallel microchannel membrane containing thousands of tunable microchannels in a format compatible with standard cell culture, imaging, cell retrieval, and direct lysis. The platform enables control over channel cross-sectional area, length, and geometry across multiple cell types. Using this system, we recovered sufficient post-confined cells for bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, revealing confinement-dependent transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility signatures. Increasing confinement was associated with predominantly reduced chromatin accessibility, while comparison of two cancer cell lines identified shared differentially expressed genes and convergent enrichment of cancer-associated, inflammatory, and EMT-related pathways. This scalable platform enables omics-scale analysis of cells after migration through defined physical microenvironments.

papers.title: Plasma-Polymerized Polyurethane/Reduced Graphene Oxide Electrospun Patch for Cardiac Tissue Engineering
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Traditional treatments, including heart transplantation, are limited by the scarcity of donor organs and the need for lifelong immunosuppression, highlighting the urgent need for alternative therapies. Cardiac patches represent a promising approach to restoring heart function by providing structural support and promoting cardiac tissue regeneration. Here, we developed biocompatible and conductive electrospun cardiac patches, aiming to mimic the structural, mechanical, and electrical properties of the native myocardium. polyurethane (PU) was selected as the base material due to its favorable mechanical properties and biocompatibility. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was incorporated into the electrospun PU fibers to enhance electrical conductivity, and a low-pressure plasma-polymerized nitrogen-rich (LPPE:N) coating was applied to improve cell adhesion. The fabricated patches were characterized through various techniques, including scanning electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, tensile testing, and conductivity measurements. Also, in vitro cytotoxicity assay using primary cardiac fibroblasts confirmed the biocompatibility of the patches. These physicochemical, electromechanical, and biological characterizations suggest that the rGO/LPPE:N-functionalized PU patches demonstrate promising potential for cardiac tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Digital light processing of human-scale tissue-engineered heart valves
papers.abstract: Tissue engineered heart valves (TEHVs) could overcome the complications of current heart valve replacement, such as immunologic events, degenerative fibrocalcific changes, and patient-prosthesis mismatch. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables creation of complex geometries; however, suitable (bio)inks remain limited. Here, a composite ink comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA), gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), and methacrylated quince seed mucilage (QSGM), termed GPQuin, was developed for DLP printing of human-scale TEHVs. GPQuin enabled fabrication of a trileaflet TEHV with separated leaflets and anatomically inspired sinuses. Micro-computed tomography revealed mean positive and negative surface deviations of +214 and -248 micrometers, respectively. The printed hydrogels exhibited a tensile modulus of 117.2 +/- 15.5 kPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 113.2 +/- 17.4 kPa, and an elongation at break of 75.3 +/- 2.3%. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived valve cells attached to the hydrogel surfaces and remained predominantly viable over 14 days. After 12 weeks of subcutaneous implantation, the constructs showed a time-dependent inflammatory response. In a pulse duplicator under pulmonary loading, printed valves exhibited good cyclic leaflet opening and closing. Together, these findings establish GPQuin as a printable platform for human-scale valve scaffolds and support further investigation in heart valve tissue engineering.

papers.title: Continuous-flow synthesis and functionalization of gold nanoparticles for diagnostics and therapy
papers.abstract: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are highly versatile platforms in nanomedicine, but their clinical translation is hin-dered by poor reproducibility and scalability during synthesis and surface functionalization, which are still pre-dominantly performed via manual batch protocols. To overcome these manufacturing bottlenecks, this work introduces a modular, continuous-flow millifluidic platform that integrates the automated synthesis of citrate-stabilized AuNPs and their subsequent multi-step surface modification within a single, streamlined pipeline. AuNPs of approximately 13 and 22 nm were reliably produced by adjusting the reagent stoichiometry. The flow-synthesized nanoconjugates showed hydrodynamic diameters comparable to those of the batch formulations, and comparable zeta potentials except for the PEG-containing ones. The platform's chemical flexibility was validated through two distinct surface modifications: an in-line covalent ligand exchange mediated by bidentate dithiolane anchors, and a salt-free, ultra-fast low-pH adsorption method. To benchmark diagnostic performance against established batch protocols, flow-modified AuNPs were evaluated in previously optimized SARS-CoV-2 RNA sensing systems, a cholesterol-driven molecular beacon assay and the CRISPR-Cas13a-mediated CAS-CADE platform, reproducing the response time, specificity, and colorimetric readout of their batch-produced counterparts without requiring tedious salt-aging steps. The same hairpin design was also adapted to a lateral flow format. For therapeutic purposes, two distinct classes of bioactive agents were evaluated: a small-molecule chemotherapeutic system co-loaded with SN38 and the nucleolin-targeting AS1411 aptamer, which exhibited potent anti-proliferative activity against triple-negative breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231), and a nucleic acid-based platform functionalized with the antisense oligonucleotide ASO34a via the low-pH module, which trig-gered significant post-transcriptional gene silencing (achieving at least 30% luciferase knockdown at 24 hours in both breast and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cell lines). This automated millifluidic platform demonstrates that complex, multi-component nanomaterial modifications can be successfully executed under continuous-flow configurations, reproducing the performance of established batch-synthesized diagnostic assays and yielding active therapeutic nanoconjugates. By coupling precise core synthesis with sophisticated surface engineering, this continuous manufacturing paradigm establishes a scalable and reproducible pathway to narrow the gap between laboratory-scale discovery and clinical manufacturing.

papers.title: VivoFemme: 3D printed human endometrium-on-chip with a thin membrane and gravity-driven perfusion
papers.abstract: Modeling endometrial function in vitro requires systems that support interactions among epithelial, stromal, and endothelial cells and allow their responses to hormonal and physical cues to be examined. Here, we present VivoFemme, an endometrium-on-chip platform that combines a capillary-pinned gelatin membrane, a stereolithographically 3D-printed microfluidic chip, and gravity-driven perfusion. Gelatin membrane retained on 3D-printed mesh supports separate independently accessible culture micro-channels. The membrane has approximately 10 micrometers thickness measured by cross-sections using scanning electron microscopy. Optimization of gelatin crosslinking conditions identified a formulation that maintained membrane integrity throughout the culture period. The microfluidic chip operates without external perfusion pumps or circulation tubing and supports primary human endometrial epithelial, stromal, and microvascular endothelial cells in mono-, co-, and tri-culture configurations. Compared with static culture, dynamic endothelial culture showed greater alignment along the flow axis and reduced permeability. Treatment with estradiol, medroxyprogesterone acetate, and cyclic adenosine monophosphate was accompanied by prolactin secretion and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 staining, consistent with stromal decidualization. Prolactin and tracer permeability measurements differed across culture configurations. VivoFemme combines a thin gelatin interface with compartmentalized culture and gravity-driven perfusion to investigate how cellular composition and culture conditions influence endometrial responses.

papers.title: Tuning viral virulence and cytokine release enforces oncotropism and eliminates systemic toxicity: A framework for next-generation oncolytics
papers.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy has long balanced safety and potency through permanent attenuation and, increasingly, constitutive inflammatory payloads. Yet attenuation can restrict replication in heterogeneous tumors, whereas unregulated cytokine expression can cause systemic toxicity and promote premature viral clearance. Here, we establish an alternative vaccinia framework that replaces fixed attenuation with reversible chemogenetic control of the essential replication gene E1L and coordinates replication with graded interleukin-12 (IL-12) expression through a hierarchical, drug-gated circuit. E1L control enabled inducible replication with no detectable consensus-level escape under tested selection conditions. Following intravenous administration, the fully induced virus maintained high intratumoral titers while reducing infectious-virus recovery across peripheral organs by orders of magnitude relative to thymidine-kinase-deleted vaccinia and the induced parent vector, without marked weight loss. Across syngeneic tumor models, dual induction prolonged survival and was associated with cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell and inflammatory macrophage states. This architecture establishes post-entry functional oncotropism through control of productive viral persistence.

papers.title: Correlative mapping links extracellular matrix architecture to local mechanics in cardiac aging
papers.abstract: Cardiac aging is accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, but how changes in matrix architecture relate to local tissue mechanics remains poorly understood. Here, we quantified six image-derived architectural descriptors across selected ECM components in young and aged murine myocardium and integrated them into an architectural index that we term 'ArchI'. Age-associated architectural changes differed among ECM components, with higher ArchI values observed for fibrillar collagen, fibronectin, and laminin-associated networks. To examine how defined structural changes affect the component descriptors, we developed controlled synthetic geometries and a stochastic network model. These analyses revealed index sensitivity to matrix occupancy, fiber width, and network continuity. We then combined nanoindentation of fresh cardiac tissue slices with subsequent immunofluorescence staining and imaging of collagen to correlate local tissue stiffness with ECM architecture in corresponding regions. Aged myocardium exhibited higher ArchI and Young's modulus, with local heterogeneity in their spatial correspondence. Age-adjusted regression revealed a positive association between ArchI and Young's modulus, with a steeper association in aged myocardium. Together, these findings reveal component-specific ECM remodeling during aging and provide a means to examine spatial structure-mechanics relationships in the aging heart.

papers.title: Beyond screens: a gaze-driven auditory human-computer interface
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces enable humans to communicate and manipulate external devices by converting physiological signals into actions. These signals often have a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) too low to enable their use in real-world Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Notably, electrooculography (EOG) measurements of gaze direction exhibit a higher SNR, making them widely employed in HCI applications with displays. Nevertheless, display-free paradigms can also leverage the high SNR of EOG measurements of eye gaze. Current auditory paradigms present options sequentially, extending stimulus presentation time and reducing the information transfer rates (ITRs) compared to visual displays. This paper introduces an HCI approach that combines the SNR of eye gaze with a rapid auditory display paradigm. This paradigm leverages the human capacity to focus on a single auditory stream presented among others. By integrating eye gaze with a rapid auditory display, our method attains average accuracies of 82.7% for a five-option menu and average peak ITRs of 41 bits/min. This increase in performance represents a stride towards practical HCIs in real-world scenarios and display-free smart devices.

papers.title: Biophysics-informed generative models improve activity and thermostability of designed ribozymes
papers.abstract: Generative models of biological sequences can produce molecules that fold and function similarly to natural ones. A further challenge is to steer generation toward a desired property, such as resistance to high temperature. This is particularly difficult when available sequence data are limited, and typically requires probing thousands of variants experimentally, either through directed evolution or to retrain a model specialized to the targeted property. Ideally, however, one would avoid such an expensive experimental step. Here, we show that biophysical information can complement limited evolutionary data to guide the design of catalytic RNA molecules toward increased activity and thermostability. We combine a sequence generative model with a physical score based on the Turner nearest-neighbor model, whose parameters were originally derived from calorimetric measurements, independently of the sequence family considered. On its own, this physical score is ineffective for design: optimizing it destroys function, likely because it is blind to the catalytic core and to tertiary contacts. However, when coupled to the generative model, it provides complementary information that enables better designs than evolutionary data alone. We demonstrate this on self-splicing group I intron ribozymes: starting from designs that are active at 37 C but inactive at 60 C, fewer than ten substitutions are sufficient to confer catalytic activity at 60 C.

papers.title: Engineering Bacteriophages to Overcome Complement-Mediated Neutralization
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are promising alternatives to antibiotics for treating antibiotic-resistant infections, but their clinical durability is limited by the host immune response against phages. Using phage T4 as a model and both C1q-KO and C3-deficient mice, we show that antibody recognition of phages triggers complement-dependent neutralization and clearance of phage particles in vivo. To mitigate this complement-mediated clearance, we engineer phages to display the complement-modulating Factor H binding peptide, a phage we call T4-FactorH.BP. Indeed, T4-FactorH.BP resists inactivation in human donor sera from individuals with pre-existing antibodies against T4 phage. Similarly, in mice immunized against T4 circulation of T4-FactorH.BP is prolonged in vivo. These results establish a critical role for the classical complement pathway in phage clearance and provide a path towards improving the pharmacokinetics of phage therapeutics in vivo by evading complement.

papers.title: Rigid granular scaffolds reveal transcriptional responses to cellular confinement
papers.abstract: A large variety of cells migrate through confined spaces in vivo, where mechanical confinement influences their fate and function. However, existing in vitro confinement models are low-throughput, limiting discovery of confinement-responsive genes and recovery of confined cells. Here, we present non-annealed glass microparticle scaffolds (GlaMS) as a scalable, high-throughput 3D confinement system with interconnected voids that mimic physiological confinement while enabling efficient cell retrieval. Using LOVAMAP, a computational tool that segments void spaces to estimate spatial constrictions, we quantified confinement levels in GlaMS and compared them with ex vivo interstitial spaces to identify the sphere size that best mimics in vivo confinement. Using human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) as a mechanosensitive cell model, confinement within GlaMS was found to induce morphological changes, accelerated migration, altered YAP signaling, and enhanced osteogenic priming after replating, demonstrating transient confinement-induced effects. Taking advantage of the high throughput capabilities of GlaMS, we performed RNAseq on populations of confined cells and identified confinement degree-dependent shifts in gene expression. TMEM158 emerged as a previously unrecognized confinement-sensitive gene, was independently validated in microchannel assays, and was found by loss-of-function analysis to contribute to efficient confined migration. Together, this work establishes GlaMS as a scalable platform for population-level confinement mechanobiology, allowing recovery and molecular profiling of cells exposed to predictable three-dimensional confinement.

papers.title: Multifunctional CNT-based Platform for Enhanced Dopaminergic Differentiation and Electrochemical Dopamine Sensing from Human iPSC-derived Neurons.
papers.abstract: Pairing neuro-electrochemical sensors with physiologically relevant neuronal models represents a new frontier in the study of neurodegenerative diseases. In this work, we reported an electroactive platform for in situ detection of dopamine, combining human iPSC-derived neurons with carbon nanotubes. In this system, carbon nanotubes served a triple role: enhancing the electroactive area, catalyzing dopamine oxidation, and promoting subtype-specific dopaminergic differentiation. We developed a robust protocol achieving functional dopaminergic neurons, confirmed via qPCR, immunocytochemistry, MEA electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. CNT substrates were associated with a significant increase in the TH/neurofilament overlap (37.90 {+/-} 3.80% vs. 26.01 {+/-} 3.75% in controls). Applying differential pulse voltammetry and chronoamperometry, we quantified extracellular dopamine at 1.25 M and confirmed the stimulus-dependent release induced by benztropine and KCl depolarization. Post-electrochemical immunostaining confirmed that neurons retained their morphology and TH expression. Overall, this work establishes a novel framework for neurodegenerative disease modeling that recapitulates key electrophysiological and neurochemical features of dopaminergic neurons, representing a powerful tool for disease modeling, drug screening, and the development of next-generation neuro-biosensors.

papers.title: Reproducible and open-source statistical shape models of the pose-normalized adult lower body: development and comparative evaluation
papers.abstract: Accurate skeletal geometry is important for subject-specific musculoskeletal modeling, but the choice of statistical representation may affect anatomical reconstruction. This study developed a reproducible workflow and compared four statistical shape model families of the pose-normalized adult lower body: pooled global, articulated shape-pose, sex-conditioned shared-basis, and independently fitted sex-specific models. Models were developed from computed-tomography-derived geometries of 20 adults and evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Model coefficients were estimated from each held-out subjects complete registered surfaces, assessing dense-surface representational generalization. Outcomes included model compactness, whole-body and bone-wise surface root-mean-square errors, and reconstruction errors for hip, knee, and ankle joint centers. A pelvis-referenced bounding-box anisotropic-scaling baseline was included as a geometric comparator. The pooled global and sex-conditioned models shared a principal-component basis and therefore identical compactness spectra, with the first component explaining 90.16% of the variance. These models provided the most consistent reconstruction performance. The articulated model had ankle and knee joint-center errors 9.1 and 5.4 mm higher, respectively, than the pooled global model. Independently fitted sex-specific models did not improve whole-body reconstruction over the pooled global or sex-conditioned models in this small cohort. Under the present evaluation, the pooled global and sex-conditioned models reduced whole-body surface errors by approximately 4.1 and 4.0 mm, respectively, relative to scaling. The pooled global model also reduced ankle and knee joint-center errors by 12.5 and 11.0 mm. These results characterize the implemented representations within the available dataset. The scaling comparison was not input matched, and sparse-input and external validation remain necessary. The accompanying LowerBodySSM workflow and interactive Companion provide a reproducible resource for further anatomical modeling and evaluation.

papers.title: Synthesis of Plasma Membrane-Enriched Nanodiscs from Giant Plasma Membrane Vesicles
papers.abstract: Nanodiscs are highly versatile biomaterials with applications in cell membrane mimicry, membrane protein (MP) characterization, and hybrid biological-abiological material synthesis. The plasma membrane (PM) is an ideal starting material for nanodisc synthesis because it naturally houses a diverse array of functionally important MPs in their native lipid environment. However, the PM comprises a small fraction of the total membrane material in a typical eukaryotic cell. Traditional methods to isolate the PM suffer from undefined relative PM enrichment compared to other cellular membranous structures. Here, we introduce a method to synthesize PM-enriched nanodiscs (PMNDs) from giant plasma membrane vesicles (GPMVs). We show that GPMV-derived PMNDs retain functional membrane-anchored protein, exhibit uniform size and morphology, and bind specifically and dose-dependently to the PM of cells expressing a cognate receptor. This strategy offers broad applicability for synthesizing nanodiscs with novel MPs for investigating PM-nanomaterial interactions, cellular targeting, and vaccine development using immunologic MPs.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.abstract: While MEG source localization pipelines often employ head models of one single compartment with homogeneous conductivity, researchers and clinicians use at least 3 different layers in head models for EEG source localization. Recent AI-based segmentation makes it possible to generate individualized head models with 40 high-resolution, non-nested tissues. We present a pipeline that can make use of, and test, these highly realistic models for EEG source localization: with the boundary element fast multipole method (BEM-FMM), we compute transcranial electric stimulation (TES) solutions on the full 40-tissue geometry and use them reciprocally to obtain the EEG leadfields. Out approach runs on a single modest workstation, requiring approximately 4.5 min per EEG channel for a mesh of about one million elements at a relative residual of 1e-4. We applied the pipeline to six participants undergoing intermittent photic stimulation at half their individual alpha peak frequency, comparing 61-channel EEG source localizations from 40-tissue and 5-layer models with each other and with localizations from simultaneously recorded MEG. We further compared noiseless synthetic EEG topographies of the two models across the entire cortex. The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighed relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with the MEG localizations within the visual cortex. The synthetic topographies also agreed closely, with differences scaling approximately linearly with the angle between the source orientations of the two models, underscoring the importance of accurate source normals in fixed-orientation source models. These results establish 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization, and open the way to applications where nested geometries cannot represent the anatomy, such as infants or patients with skull defects, injuries, or tumors.

papers.title: Internalizing-peptide engineering converts blocking anti-EGFR antibodies into EGFR lysosomal targeting degraders
papers.abstract: Conventional antibodies targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) primarily inhibit receptor activation rather than efficiently eliminating the receptor from tumor cells. Here, we investigated whether engineering full-length anti-EGFR antibodies with internalizing peptides could promote receptor degradation, enhance their biological activity and enable the development of recombinant receptor-depleting antibodies. Chemical conjugation of cetuximab (CTX) to the polyarginine peptide R12 enhanced intracellular uptake, reduced surface-accessible EGFR and decreased total receptor abundance in vitro. CTX-R12 conjugate also enhanced inhibition of wound repopulation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines, an effect reproduced using the R12 variant LINC18, and transferred to the independent blocking anti-EGFR antibody LEI. Incorporation of LINC19, a variant of LINC18, into recombinant full-length antibody fusion proteins preserved their activity. The LEI-LINC19 fusion (LEIP), reduced surface-accessible and total EGFR, with bafilomycin A1 reversing receptor loss and supporting an acidification-dependent endolysosomal component of degradation. Functional studies indicated that the antibody-peptide reduced DNA synthesis rate. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated EGFR depletion increased TKI-associated reductions in cellular biomass in PC9 cells and increased gefitinib responsiveness in H1975 cells. Consistently, combining LEIP with either osimertinib or gefitinib produced greater inhibition of H1975 wound repopulation than the corresponding individual treatments. LDH analysis revealed increased membrane-damage-associated LDH release following LEIP-gefitinib treatment but no additional increase with LEIP-osimertinib relative to osimertinib alone. These effects extended to 3D NSCLC models. CTX-R12 inhibited PC9 3D colony development, whereas LEIP restricted expansion of established PC9 colonies and reduced the projected area of H1975 spheroids. In H1975 spheroids initiated with 1,000 or 5,000 cells per well, LEIP-containing combinations with osimertinib or gefitinib produced greater inhibition of the spheroid size than the corresponding TKI-only treatments. Nuclear Green DCS1 staining revealed no detectable baseline core necrosis in untreated H1975 spheroids, whereas LEIP treatment was associated with DNA-positive material within and surrounding the spheroids. Moreover, LEIP-treated H1975 spheroids exhibited markedly reduced EGFR immunofluorescence compared with control and parental LEI-treated spheroids. Together, these findings demonstrate that internalizing-peptide engineering of blocking anti- EGFR antibodies can generate full-length EGFR-depleting fusion proteins with enhanced biological activity. The recombinant LEIP format and its activity in 3D in vitro NSCLC tumor models support further investigation of fusion antibody-mediated EGFR degradation as a complementary strategy to EGFR kinase inhibition.

papers.title: Myosin II-FAK-paxillin Signaling Governs Mechanosensitive Responses of Neuronal Cells to Magnetic Stimulation
papers.abstract: Recent work has highlighted transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as a promising, non-invasive therapeutic approach for a variety of diseases such as Parkinsons disease (PD). Magnetic stimulation (MS) causes action potentials that result in dopamine release and increases in neuroplasticity. While secretion and the electrophysiology of MS have been well characterized, other downstream effects of MS are unknown. Here we characterize a mechanotransduction pathway that is activated in response to MS in a dopaminergic cell line (N27-A). Integrin tension was measured using DNA-based integrin tension sensors (ITSs), and cytoskeletal and focal adhesion structure was quantified in response to pharmacological inhibitors and activators of common mechanotransduction pathways. MS enhances ITS rupture in N27-A cells in a dose dependent manner. Additionally, both pulse frequency and number control ITS rupture. The ITS rupture that MS causes occurs through both cell migration-independent and -dependent mechanisms. Furthermore, MS enhances integrin forces in N27-A cells through a myosin II- and FAK-dependent pathway by creating more internal adhesions with increased phosphorylated paxillin. This work definitively demonstrates that MS can cause robust changes in mechanotransduction, which likely regulate neuroplasticity and provide an addition mechanism to explain the efficacy and potential of TMS therapy.

papers.title: Interspecies differences in lamina cribrosa fiber composition and architecture might arise from differences in optic nerve head size and mechanical constraints
papers.abstract: The lamina cribrosa (LC) is a complex network of fibers that plays an important mechanical role in protecting optic nerve axons as they exit the eye. Both the architecture and composition of the LC network varies throughout animal species. However, the function of these differences between species is unknown. We hypothesize that this variety in LC architecture and composition is a result of species-specific adaptations to the mechanical constraints present in each species' optic nerve head. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel optimization framework to systematically derive optimal LC fiber architecture and composition under different mechanical constraints. We then compared predicted LC architectures to instant polarized light microscopy images of actual human, tree shrew, monkey, cow, pig, and rat LCs. Distinct features from the various LCs were replicated by varying the mechanical constraints, consistent with our hypothesis. The wheel-and-spoke architecture of the tree shrew LC was captured with angularly symmetric loading conditions. Non-radial fibers like those found in monkey and human LCs were captured by adding horizontal eye rotation tractions. The softer glial LC of the rat and stiffer collagenous LC of larger species were replicated by a two-material extension of the model. To our knowledge, these are the first results that systematically show how interspecies differences in LC architecture and composition can arise from mechanical constraints and size. This work can result in better interpretation of animal models and provide a point of comparison for changes in LC architecture under pathological conditions such as glaucoma.

papers.title: CorridorKit: Open-source software for geometric comparison of skull base surgical corridors
papers.abstract: CorridorKit is open-source research software for comparing rigid surgical access corridors in physical image coordinates. Its Python engine represents finite instruments, circular portals, target samples, and protected geometry, and keeps evaluated paths linked to their reached samples, insertion depths, and clearance states through command-line, desktop, and 3D Slicer interfaces. In a reproducible 413-sample phantom, two portals reached 94 and 267 samples, with 326 in their union. Numerical verification included 82 analytical angular comparisons and 4,720 voxel-distance queries. In a public sellar CT example, conditional target coverage rose from 0 to 533 of 536 voxels as the modeled sphenoidotomy opening radius increased from 4 to 8 mm.

papers.title: Mass Transfer Formulations Shape Oxygen Transport and Tissue Oxygenation in Microvascular Networks
papers.abstract: Continuous oxygen delivery is essential for cerebral tissue function, yet its local supply characteristics remain incompletely understood. Quantifying oxygen transport in microvascular networks (MVNs) requires a physiologically consistent description of oxygen exchange between vascular compartments via mass transfer coefficients (MTCs). We investigate how different MTC formulations influence oxygen availability and hypoxic burden in realistic MVNs, and whether they produce relevant local differences in tissue oxygenation. A multicompartment oxygen transport model describing exchange between red blood cells (RBCs), plasma, and tissue in realistic MVNs was developed and evaluated against in vivo measurements. Three RBC-plasma MTC formulations were compared: constant, hematocrit-dependent, and hematocrit- and saturation-dependent. Additionally, a double-flux formulation incorporating a direct RBC-to-tissue flux was compared with standard single-flux formulations. Global tissue oxygen distributions were comparable across RBC-plasma MTC formulations, but hematocrit- and saturation-dependent MTC formulations predicted larger hypoxic tissue fractions. The largest differences occurred under low hematocrit, with local plasma oxygen partial pressure PO2 differing by {approx}6 mmHg along representative vascular paths. Introducing the direct RBC-tissue exchange reduced tissue PO2 at low hematocrit and enhanced it at high hematocrit, with the largest differences observed in small vessels. Sensitivity analysis revealed that RBC oxygen diffusivity can alter the double-flux effect magnitude. MTC assumptions substantially influence predicted oxygen availability and hypoxic burden, particularly under low-hematocrit conditions and in small vessels, underlining the need for their accurate definition. The proposed model provides a basis for evaluating these effects, improving the interpretation of oxygen transport predictions in realistic MVNs.

papers.title: A midnight snack for spirulina: a dual-substrate kinetic model for second cheese whey supplementation of Arthrospira platensis
papers.abstract: Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) is a widely used strategic cyanobacterium whose cultivation cost remains a primary barrier to large-scale production. Mixotrophic growth on dairy by-products offers a simultaneous route to increase biomass concentration and valorize industrial waste streams. Here, we investigate the effect of Parmigiano Reggiano second cheese whey supplementation on A. platensis batch cultivation under continuous and alternating photoperiods. Whey supplementation increased final biomass in a dose-dependent manner under both continuous and alternating light. At the higher supplementation level, cultures under alternating light reached the same final biomass as under continuous illumination within the cultivation window. To interpret the interaction between whey availability, photoperiod, and biomass accumulation, we developed a kinetic model in which inorganic substrate assimilation is light-dependent, while whey-associated growth can contribute during both light and dark phases through a phenomenological dark-phase coefficient. Model and experimental results are consistent with the assumption that photoperiod mainly modulates the rate of biomass accumulation rather than the attainable biomass, under sufficient substrate availability. These results support a nutrient-stoichiometric interpretation of the biomass ceiling and suggest that second cheese whey supplementation can reduce dependence on continuous artificial lighting, providing a promising route for more resource-efficient Arthrospira cultivation.
